name: PowerShell started by a remote-execution service
description: Lab rule 1 of 3 for the CTIA cryptomining-001 scenario, and the one the alert is named after. A PowerShell process whose parent is the WMI provider host is the delivery step of a cryptomining infection - something remote told that server to fetch and run a file. It fires exactly once in this dataset, which is the point of the lab: cryptomining is low-and-slow and a rule written against the noise a miner makes stays quiet. The query is the same one guided-walkthrough.html asks for by hand, narrowed to the one row that matters. The time window is deliberately long because this lab ships historical data - a lab-only concession, not a production setting; a real deployment would decode the -EncodedCommand payload, alert on any wmiprvse.exe parent, and treat a service account creating a process as worth a look on its own.
